To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is species-specificity in magnitude and duration of stress response in Mediterranean cultured fish and the method of measuring cortisol concentration in rearing water can be used for stress monitoring.
the stress response of cultured Mediterranean fish is species specific and the method of measuring cortisol in rearing water is a useful tool for the assessment of stress in cultured marine fish.

(1) The species-specific stress response is a very useful tool in order to evaluate the stress sensitivity of marine fish species in aquaculture, and (2) the free cortisol released rate to the rearing water, is a reliable and non-invasive method for monitoring stress in marine species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the species-specificity of the stress response and the use of free cortisol concentration in rearing water as an indicator of stress in cultured marine fish.
the development of a non-invasive method for stress assessment and monitoring in marine fish species of aquaculture interest.

the identification of the species-specific response to acute stress and the development of a non-invasive method to measure the magnitude and duration, which can be used in aquaculture management and in environmental monitoring. © Inter-Research 2008.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress response of each species is different and the magnitude and duration are dependent upon the species.
the stress responses of the studied species are not similar, and therefore the stress response in marine fish should be considered on a species basis.
the species-specificity in magnitude and duration of stress response in marine fishes is a general phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are clear species-specific responses to stress, and the magnitude of these responses is related to the degree of stress tolerance of a species.
the magnitude of the stress response is species-specific, while the duration of the stress is not.
the species-specific stress responses in terms of plasma glucose and cortisol are not necessarily related to their relative stress resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
species-specificity in stress response must be considered when designing experiments and interpreting results.
species-specific stress responses should be considered when evaluating the stress response of cultured species.
the stress response in marine fishes is highly species-dependent and therefore it is not possible to generalize stress effects in different species.
